'''Arvydas Macijauskas''' (born 19 January 1980) is a Lithuanian former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|m=1.93}} tall, he played at the [[shooting guard]] position. Widely considered one of the greatest Lithuanian players of the 2000s, he won numerous individual awards, as well as [[sports club|club]] and [[national sports team|national team]] titles.

After starting his professional career with [[BC Neptūnas|Neptūnas]], he later played for some top [[EuroLeague]] teams, such as [[Saski Baskonia|Tau Ceramica]] and [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. He also played with the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans/Oklahoma City Hornets]] for one season in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. He also represented the senior [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuanian national basketball team]].

He announced his retirement from playing professional basketball in 2010, two years after his last club, [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], had released him following a prolonged judicial litigation.

==Early career==
Early in his career, Macijauskas was a member of the [[BC Neptūnas|Neptūnas]] junior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=CBV |title=Arvydas Macijauskas Career Notes |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=1980-01-19 |access-date=2012-01-25}}</ref>

==Professional playing career==
===Lithuania===
Macijauskas made his [[professional sports|pro]] debut in 1997, during the 1996–97 season, with the [[Lithuanian Basketball League|Lithuanian League]] club [[BC Neptūnas|Neptūnas]]. He only played in 3 games in his rookie season, and spent most of the season with the [[Klaipėda University]]-Irvinga team. He spent three seasons with Neptūnas, and averaged 12.7 points per game, on 53 percent field goal shooting, in the Lithuanian League.

He played the next four seasons with the Lithuanian club [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos rytas]], and he led them to two Lithuanian League titles, in 2000 and 2002, and to a [[Northern European Basketball League|Northern European League]] title in 2003. He was named the [[Lithuanian Basketball League Finals MVP|Lithuanian League Finals MVP]] in 2002 and 2003. He averaged 15.3 points per game, on 61 percent field goal shooting, in 143 games played with Rytas.

On 11 November 2023, Rytas Vilnius retired Macijauskas' jersey No. 7.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.delfi.lt/krepsinis/naujienos/arenos-palube-vilniuje-papuose-macijausko-marskineliai-susigraudines-legendinis-snaiperis-dekojo-sirgaliams-95040911|title=Arenos palubę Vilniuje papuošė Macijausko marškinėliai, susigraudinęs legendinis snaiperis dėkojo sirgaliams|website=DELFI |language=lt}}</ref>

===Spain===
Macijauskas joined the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] club [[Saski Baskonia|Tau Ceramica]], for the next two seasons and he helped them win a [[Spanish Basketball King's Cup|Spanish Cup]] title in [[2004 Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|2004]]. On 17 December 2003 he scored a career-high 40 points, in a [[2003–04 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2003–04 season]] game against the [[LNB Pro A|French League]] club [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Lyon]]. With Tau Ceramica, he also reached the EuroLeague's [[2005 EuroLeague Final Four|Final in 2005]], where his team lost to the [[Israeli Basketball Super League|Israeli Super League]] club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]; which was also led by a [[Lithuania]]n player, and [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]], [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]]. Macijauskas was selected to the [[All-EuroLeague]] First Team of the [[2004–05 Euroleague|2004–05 season]]. In two seasons with Tau, he played in 42 [[EuroLeague]] games, in which he averaged 18.6 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game.

===NBA===
Macijauskas signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans/Oklahoma City Hornets]] in 2005. He was rarely used in his only season in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], as he totaled 135 minutes of playing time, and 44 points scored, in 19 games played.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/historical/playerfile/index.html?player=arvydas_macijauskas |title=Arvydas Macijauskas Info Page |work=NBA.com |date=1980-01-19 |access-date=2012-01-25}}</ref> He was bought out by the Hornets after the season ended. After returning to Europe, he criticized the Hornets and the NBA through the press. When asked if he had put the previous season behind him, Macijauskas responded: "I want to forget that year. Everything went wrong. A really bad coach, a bad franchise. At the end of the season, I didn't even think of returning to New Orleans next season. From the third game on, I was already sentenced to zero minutes for the rest of the year. The NBA is not a fun experience. Teams are (not) teams. There's no true commitment between the teammates."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/article/2962273/ |title=Macijauskas mouthing off again |publisher=Newsok.com |date=2006-10-27 |access-date=2012-01-25}}</ref>

===Greece===
On 20 July 2006 Macijauskas signed with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. The deal was worth [[euro sign|€]]9 million euros [[net income]] over four years. However, he suffered a devastating [[Achilles' tendon]] injury in September 2006, and he only played in two games during the [[2006–07 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2006–07 season]].

Macijauskas was healthy for the following [[2007–08 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2007–08 season]], and he was named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month]] for November 2007, after shooting a staggering 72.5 percent overall from the field (84.6 percent on 2 point field goal attempts, and 50 percent on 3 point field goal attempts). Olympiacos lost to the eventual EuroLeague champions [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], in the league's quarterfinals. Ironically, one of that team's leaders was also a [[Lithuania]]n player, [[Ramūnas Šiškauskas]].

Later that year, Olympiacos sued Macijauskas for violating his contract terms (he injured his ankle during a holiday). The club wanted to cancel his contract, without paying him anymore compensation.<ref>[http://www.talkbasket.net/news/trial-macijauskas-vs.-olympiacos-postponed.html Trial Macijauskas vs. Olympiacos postponed] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081211014100/http://www.talkbasket.net/news/trial-macijauskas-vs.-olympiacos-postponed.html |date=December 11, 2008 }}</ref> A court later made a decision in Macijauskas' favor. However, Olympiacos appealed it, and eventually won the case in November 2009.<ref>[http://www.talkbasket.net/news/olympiacos-wins-macijauskas-case-2432.html Olympiacos wins "Macijauskas case" ] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091115074239/http://www.talkbasket.net/news/olympiacos-wins-macijauskas-case-2432.html |date=November 15, 2009 }}</ref> In two seasons with Olympiacos, he played in 14 EuroLeague games, in which he averaged 13.8 points and 2.1 rebounds per game.

In June 2010, he announced his retirement from his basketball playing career, because of health reasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/72432/180 |title=Shooting star Macijauskas ends comeback try |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=2010-06-09 |access-date=2012-01-25}}</ref>

==National team career==
Macijauskas was a member of the [[Lithuania national under-18 basketball team|Lithuanian Under-18]] and [[Lithuania national under-20 basketball team|Under-20]] junior national teams. He played at the [[1998 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] and at the [[2000 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]].

Macijauskas led the senior [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania national team]] in scoring, at the [[EuroBasket 2003]], with an average of 15.8 points per game. The Lithuanians prevailed to win the gold medals at the tournament. However, his teammate, [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]], was named [[EuroBasket MVP|the tournament's MVP]].

He also played at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympic Games]], where the Lithuanians finished in fourth place. He averaged 15.9 points per game, on 54 percent field goal shooting, and scored a tournament-high 32 points against [[China national basketball team|China]], in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.basketball.doudiz.com/match/432090.html |title=Lithuania 95, China 75 Boxscore |publisher=En.basketball.doudiz.com |date=2004-08-26 |access-date=2012-01-25 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120216175731/http://en.basketball.doudiz.com/match/432090.html |archive-date=2012-02-16 }}</ref>

Macijauskas also played at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship|2006 World Championship]], where the Lithuanian team finished in seventh place. He was a candidate for the Lithuanian team for [[EuroBasket 2009]] in Poland, but at the last minute, he declared that he would not participate in the tournament.<ref>[http://www.delfi.lt/news/sport/eurobasket2003/article.php?id=23144114 Delfi.lt - A. Macijausko rinktinėje nebus] {{in lang|lt}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 19 June 2010 Macijauskas became the assistant [[basketball coach|coach]] of the Lithuanian club [[Perlas (basketball club)|Perlas Vilnius]],<ref>http://sportas.delfi.lt/eurobasket2003/nzabarausko-asistentu-perlo-komandoje-dirbs-amacijauskas.d?id=34620825 N. Zabarauskas' assistant will be A. Macijauskas {{in lang|lt}}</ref> but in August it was announced that he had left Perlas, for personal reasons.

==Personal life==
Arvydas Macijauskas married Viktorija Buder on 24 July 2010.<ref>{{cite web|author=Snieguolė Dovidavičienė |url=https://www.alfa.lt/straipsnis/10379504/?Krepsininkas.Macijauskas.vede=2010-07-24_12-38 |title=Krepsininkas.Macijauskas.vede |language=lt |publisher=Alfa.lt |date=2010-07-24 |access-date=2012-01-25}}</ref>
